frames.review_note: Minor: a few small puddles on the laterite rampart floor suggest earlier rain, while the caption says the rain had not yet fallen. They read as old monsoon wet, so this is acceptable. Low dark-bellied clouds, flat husk-fire smoke along the beach and three small grey ships at anchor all match the script. No text in the art. The wide cloud band at the top leaves room for the caption.

Minor: the surf shows some whitecaps rather than truly sluggish waves, but the haze and still palms carry the heavy-air beat. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a gold ear stud. He is in three-quarter back view on the same laterite rampart, with the same domed sentry turret as 1.1. The grey sky on the upper right has room for both captions.

Minor: the ground at the gate is puddled, which hints at rain, though dripping seawater and earlier monsoon wet can explain it. The cousin has a beard, which the script does not forbid. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, grey-flecked beard, short teal coat over a cream vest with bulging pockets, the scar on his LEFT side from ear to jaw, short and broad, and grinning. He wrings teal coat cloth at his cuff while water drips, and his hands are sound. The cousin is taller and thinner, bare-chested in a checked lungi, with no coat and no scar. The fort gate is the same laterite as 1.1 and 1.2. The sky on the upper right has room for the caption.

Usable tight insert: an aged hand in plain white cloth holds an iron stylus still over a corded palm leaf on a low wooden desk on a woven mat, with a brass oil lamp. No face is shown, so there is nothing to check against Ramayyan's sheet beyond the hand and white cloth, and both fit. The lower 40% of the frame is plain dark wood, a clean place for both captions. Small faults: (1) the incised rows are tally-like pseudo-glyphs rather than plain fine lines, and a few strokes look letter-like ('a', 'e', 'r') under zoom, but nothing is legible and at reading size they read as scratched entries in a list; (2) the stylus tip touches the leaf at the end of a row instead of hovering just above a name, though it still reads as a point that has stopped; (3) the warm lamplight mood differs from the prompt's grey overcast daylight, which matters little for an insert; (4) under close zoom the middle fingertip on each side of the stylus looks slightly doubled, which cannot be seen at print size.

Minor only: the background banners carry a gold elephant on red rather than the Travancore silver conch (no lettering), and the courtyard stones look damp under overcast haze, with no falling rain visible. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud. Ramayyan matches his sheet and keeps his eyes on the leaf. The red laterite wall above Ramayyan and to the right of Nagoji's head leaves ample space for both balloons in reading order.

Minor only: she is stepping over the threshold rather than standing and leaning in the doorway, but she is still in the doorway, using the stick, with a dry half-smile that fits 'not quite a laugh'. She matches her sheet and the bible: thick black hair coiled at the nape with no grey, a gold ball earring and bead necklace, the cream sari with a gold border in the Kerala drape with no blouse, and the long stick. Hands and feet are sound and there is no text. The large plain laterite wall on the right (about x 0.60 to 0.95, y 0.05 to 0.55) takes both balloons easily.

Minor only: there is a faint stipple of skin texture on Nagoji's jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven, and Ramayyan's writing desk is doubled into two stacked low tables. Nagoji matches the bible: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging from it, long curly black hair, cream tunic and red sash. His eyes turn toward Ramayyan, who keeps writing with a stylus on a palm-leaf bundle. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, no marks. The brass lamp has an open wick and there is no text. The plain laterite wall at upper right (about x 0.60 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.30) gives clean space for the caption.

None significant. The insert is tight on the leaf: a long, narrow palm-leaf strip with fine incised lines only and no script, held in Padmini's left hand. A braided red cord with a small round lac seal hangs from a hole at the far end, and the seal shows no letters. Her right hand grips the stick, and both hands have the right number of fingers and sound anatomy. The cream and gold sari and gold bangles match her sheet. The room and the overcast doorway continue panel 2.2. The plain dark laterite wall at upper right (about x 0.62 to 0.92, y 0.02 to 0.28) holds both captions without covering the hand or the leaf.

Forced pick past the two-correction stopping rule (Claude, 2026-10-08). v04 is a hand retouch of v02 (see HAND-RETOUCH-2026-10-08.json): Padmini alone in the anteroom, on model, eyes on the middle distance, leaf lowered, clear wall for both balloons. The faint pseudo-text on the leaf is smoothed away. Remaining fault for the author: the leaf is a short, broad tag with a pale cord, not the long narrow ola strip with the red braided cord of 2.4.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the commander sheet and the ch13 row: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, a clean chin with only faint shading, a tiny flush gold ear stud, cream tunic with sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash, brass-hilted sword as on his sheet, and boots. Padmini matches her sheet. The setting is a laterite rampart under midday overcast light, with Dutch ships at anchor offshore. Men below along the wall haul cannon on ropes beside stacked shot. Flags are plain red with no marks. There is no text and the anatomy is sound. Deviations: Nagoji walks nearly level beside her rather than a full pace behind. The tip of her stick runs out of the bottom of the frame instead of being shown on the stone. Her right hand hangs close to Nagoji's scabbard tip, a slight tangent that still reads as depth. Lettering: the large open sky at upper right easily takes both small Padmini balloons. The 3.4 inset should go in the lower-right corner, over the wall and shot, not the lower left, where Nagoji's boots are.

Acceptable for a small hands-only inset. Padmini's cream sari with its gold border, her gold bangle and her stick hand identify her. Her other hand rests on folded bolts of cloth while soldiers' wives take cloth and a measure of rice from the baskets in a laterite storeroom, with the fort visible through the doorway. That is the afternoon beat. Every hand is sound: four hands on the measure and the cloth, each traced to a wrist and arm. The flag in the doorway carries only a dark emblem, with no lettering. Minor: the cropped wife at upper right shows a short rust-red sleeve under her green drape, likely a stitched blouse. It is small and cropped at inset size, so it is noted but tolerated. Padmini's face is out of frame, so her balloon tail points to the top edge above her neckline (upper left). Lettering: the plain laterite wall at top centre, between the cloth stacks and the doorway.

Acceptable. Padmini in close-up matches her sheet: thick black hair coiled at the nape (the faint silvery lines read as sheen, not grey), gold stud earring and bead necklace, cream sari with a gold border in the old drape with no blouse, gold bangle, hand on her stick. Her face is lit warm orange by the last light. She looks right, past the frame, toward the sea and the setting sun. The setting is the same as 3.5 (Nair house with brass lamps, jackfruit tree over the stone platform, horse lines at the compound wall). There is no text and the hand is sound. Minor: one horse in the line at far right is white or grey, while the horse line in 3.5 is all dark, and the bible keeps greys out of the Madurai troop. It is small and at the frame edge. Lettering: the open orange sky at upper right, between the jackfruit foliage and the sun, takes both Padmini balloons, with tails running left to her mouth.

Minor. Nagoji's ear ornament sits as a tiny gold bead just below the lobe. At 6x zoom it reads as a small drop rather than a flush stud. It is about 7 px tall in the frame and reads as a gold dot at panel size, but it is a known stud deviation to list for the author. Everything else fixes the r1 failure. Every Madurai rider wears a white high-wrapped turban and white jama, carries a bamboo lance and rides a dark horse, with no green turban anywhere. The Maravar riders are bare-headed with curly hair, short dark jackets and hitched white mundus, on lighter, smaller ponies. Nagoji leads on the right in his rust turban, cream tunic, red sash and boots, with sleeves to the wrist, a clean chin and a curled moustache. Kayal is an ochre bay with a black mane, tail and lower legs, and no white. The scene is overcast, with hooves in the shallow wash and palms inland. The whole upper-left sky is open for three captions.

Minor. Ponnan's pony has a small white star on the forehead and is a lighter chestnut-bay than the dark-bay pony in 4.2. With no other horse in frame, it does not read as especially small. His jacket is black with gold trim, matching his sheet's trim but differing from 4.2's plain brown. Ponnan matches his sheet: bare-headed, short curly hair, heavy jaw, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, white mundu, bare feet in the stirrups. He is alone on the beach, gaze off toward the sea. The open overcast sky on the right takes his balloon easily.

Minor only: topknots sit on the crown rather than at the front, and one torch burns in daylight. Otherwise it shows the beat: bare-chested Nairs in white mundus cleaning muskets, powder flask, talisman tied on an upper arm, one muttering over his hands, one laughing with head thrown back, shields and swords stacked. Plain unlettered flags. The cloudy sky across the top leaves room for the caption.

Nagoji matches the sheet: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, sleeves to the wrists, red sash, boots, talwar. He crouches among young bare-chested Nairs who have muskets across their knees, and his hands are sound. Minor: three tiny out-of-focus figures in the gateway (around x 0.82, y 0.33) wear brimmed European-looking hats. They are barely legible at print size. The cloudy sky top-left and top-centre is clear for the balloon.

Clean. The young bare-chested Nair with a topknot laughs nervously, hand behind his head and musket held upright. The courtyard and gatehouse match 5.1 and 5.2, and the hands are sound. Minor: the topknot sits on the crown, and the muskets read as flintlocks across the page. The open sky above and left of him has room for both balloons.

Minor only: light stipple texture on Nagoji's jaw reads as shading, not a beard. The second Nair wears his topknot on the crown, not at the front. Lettering space is the grey sky band across the top left and centre, which is narrower than ideal but fits two short balloons above the heads. Otherwise clean: Nagoji matches the sheet (rust turban, curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, sleeves down, boots, talwar) and turns toward an unsmiling, bare-chested older Nair who holds a matchlock upright between his knees. The setting is the laterite courtyard with a tiled gatehouse under grey cloud. No text, no doubles, and the hands are sound.

Minor only: faint stipple on the chin and jaw (smooth enough to read as clean-shaven). The background is simplified rather than strongly blurred, but it still reads as soft and secondary. Close on Nagoji with a set jaw: rust turban, thick curled moustache, flush gold ear stud, long curly black hair, cream tunic and red sash. The courtyard with Nair soldiers, matchlocks and shields matches 5.4. The large grey-sky area at the upper right easily holds the three Nagoji balloons without touching his face.

Clean. A tight inset. A hand in a white cloth sleeve, read as Ramayyan's, pinches a small plain copper coin with no readable face onto the inked coast mark, beside a pointing index finger from the right (Varma's tracing finger). The map is lines and stipple only, with pebble and shell tokens and no lettering. Minor: Ramayyan's hand looks more weathered than 'thin', but the anatomy is sound. Plain cloth in the upper right holds the caption.

Clean. A full-width strip of a line of bullock carts on solid wooden wheels, heaped with roped pepper sacks, climbs a red-earth ghat road. Merchants in white mundus and shoulder cloths walk beside the wheels. An empty grey sea lies far behind on the left, with no ships, horses or spoked wagons. A wide, quiet overcast sky across the top third holds the voice-over box. Most merchants are seen from behind, so no face is truly readable; the listed heads are the nearest ones. RAMAYYAN (voice-over) is lettered as a tailless box under the script's notes, so the tail point (left edge, toward the coast and the war hall) is only nominal.

Acceptable, and it fixes the r1 failure: no blue coats, tricornes or other Europeans appear anywhere on land. The wide, distant view of Colachel shows burning tiled and thatched roofs with smoke columns, Dutch ships offshore with gun flashes, and townsfolk with bullock carts, baskets and children streaming up a palm road. A few bare-chested Nair men in white mundus, with topknots and long guns, walk among them. There is no text, signature, blood or bodies, and no visible anatomy faults; every figure is seen from behind, so no faces can be read. The large grey sky in the upper right is clear for both captions. Minor points: the palette is muted blue-grey rather than strongly desaturated, the muzzle flashes are bigger than 'small', and there are shot-splash columns around the ships. None of these breaks the beat.

Clean. Longboats are beaching at dawn under cannon smoke from the ships; VOC soldiers in blue coats and tricornes wade ashore; the Nair soldiers are bare-chested, in white mundus tied short, with front topknots and long guns, falling back into the dunes and palms. No text, blood or bad anatomy. The upper-left sky is clear for both captions. The palette is a little warmer than 7.1 and 7.3 but still muted.

Acceptable, and it addresses the r1 rejection. Tengapattanam is seen from a rocky shore at a great distance: burned palm-thatch frames and a Kerala-style tiled temple roof with blackened, scorched patches, smoke drifting over the water. There is no stone fort, bastion, castle or lighthouse. A single longboat pulls toward an anchored ship, carrying veiled women and small children seen from behind, rowed by two standing men in drab tunics (not red coats). There is no text on the ship or anywhere else, and no blood, ropes or chains. The open upper-right sky gives ample room for both Ramayyan memory balloons. Minor points: the oars are dipped rather than rising, the women's head veils read slightly generic, and the foreground rocks are heavy. Ramayyan is off-panel narrating from the present, so the tail points are nominal: the lower-left edge, toward the viewer's shore position, matching the off-panel convention used in 7.5.

Clean. This is a full-width strip: ships under full sail standing out to sea with plain tricolour flags and no lettering, and a thin line of blue-coated VOC soldiers on the beach watching them go beside the unfinished mud wall, cannon and awning. It matches 7.4's fort, so the page stays consistent. A wide open sky across the top holds both Karl memory boxes. The palette is somewhat bluer and brighter than a strict desaturated flashback, but in line with 7.4. Karl is off-panel and his lines are tailless memory boxes, so the tail points are nominal (lower-left edge, toward where his inset sat in 7.4).

Acceptable. Laterite wall, low tiled roofs, long rows of open-wick lamps, worshippers cupping the flames and one man pressing his palms to his eyes, thin rain at night. The upper centre-right sky is clear for the caption, and there is no painted text. Minor points for the author: the foreground woman (and two in the background) wear short-sleeved stitched blouses. The bible bans stitched blouses only for Padmini, but they are doubtful for 1740s Kerala. There is also one tiny background figure at the right edge (about x 0.83, y 0.68) in a dark coat and trousers.

Acceptable. Padmini matches her sheet: cream sari with gold border in the old drape, no blouse, gold necklace and earrings, walking stick, hair coiled at the nape. She hands a red packet to a bare-chested Nair soldier in a short white mundu. A second soldier has a white packet tied at his wrist. The Madurai riders (white high turbans, white jamas, dark horses, plain lances) hang back at the edge of the light. Minor: her tray of packets rests against her waist with no hand under it. The Nair topknots sit on the crown rather than at the front. The soldiers carry spears and swords, not matchlocks. There is a small dot on Padmini's forehead that is not on her sheet. The panel has no lettering.

Acceptable. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, vest with pockets, striped shawl, sandals. He crouches and sets a brass lamp on the lowest step among the others. Nagoji crouches beside him and matches the bible: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots and talwar. Only the outer side of his left forearm shows, so the brand stays hidden. Ibrahim's scarred left cheek is turned away. Minor: his other hand also touches a second brass lamp. The top-centre sky (x 0.35 to 0.6, y 0 to 0.25) is clear for both balloons.

Acceptable. Raza Khan matches his sheet: green high-wrapped turban, hawk nose, pointed moustache, goatee, scar on the anatomical left cheek, green drape. He raises his palms in prayer, looking toward the sea, with his Madurai men in white turbans and jamas standing apart with dark horses. Minor: two lances stand upright on the paving with no one holding them. Raza's lips are closed, not visibly moving. The top-left and top-centre sky is clear for the caption.

Acceptable. Nagoji and Ibrahim are seen from behind, looking out over the temple wall at the dark sea, with the tiny lights of three distant ships. Costumes match panel 3. Nagoji's ear stud and moustache tip show in lost profile. Minor: Ibrahim has a small gold ear stud that is not on his sheet, and he turns toward Nagoji rather than out to sea. The large open sky in the upper half holds all three balloons easily.

Minor: the father's fingertips rest on the child's forehead and hair rather than clearly tracing the face. Everything else in the beat is there: the wide estate at night, the woman at the rice jar, folded white cloth on the shelf behind her, and the jackfruit tree and horse lines that match 10.2 to 10.5. The lamps have open wicks, there is no painted text, and the night sky in the upper centre is clear for the caption.

Minor: he grips a short sheathed sword held upright rather than the bare talwar across his knees from 10.2, and the lamplight from below is soft rather than strong. Nagoji is on-model: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with only slight shading, small gold ear stud and the rust-red turban, with a clear corner-of-the-mouth smile. The dark sky at upper right takes both balloons without touching his face.

Minor: Dhanaji sits on the edge of the stone tree platform instead of the low stool from 10.2. A small brass hanging lamp in the background could read as glass-globed, but it is tiny and off the main action. He matches his sheet (short black beard, white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, no sash), the whetstone is pressed on the blade, his expression is serious, and his hands are sound. Nagoji is off-panel to the right, where he sits in 10.2. Both balloons fit in the night sky between the tree and the roof, top centre to top right.

Minor: Dhanaji's look reads more wary than softened, with a furrowed brow as he glances up to the left. He sits on a stone ledge rather than 10.2's low stool, but he squats in 10.5 too, so the page is already inconsistent there. Otherwise he matches the sheet: white pagdi, short black beard, indigo quilted tunic, no sash, gold hoop. The blade lies across his lap, and the brass lamp has an open wick on the ground. Hands are sound and there is no text. The night sky at upper right is clear for both balloons.

Minor: this is a medium shot of the seated Nagoji with his chin on his fist, not a tight face shot, and Keshavrao reaches upward as he goes under rather than plainly sinking. The beat still reads. The storm-water memory bleeds in from the left. A rope runs through bandaged palms and its frayed end whips loose, tied to no one. Keshavrao has hacked short hair, a faint moustache, rags and paired ankle chains, and no rope comes near his neck or body. Nagoji is on-model: thick moustache, clean chin, gold stud, rust-red turban, red sash, boots, sleeves down. The caption can sit on the low-detail ground at lower left or in the top-centre sky. Nagoji's balloon fits over the dim house and sky left of his head.

Clean. In this full-width strip Padmini, with her stick, walks ahead of Nagoji toward a dark thicket at right that looms like an island. They pass raised wooden granaries on stone footings with tiled roofs, under a starry, cloudy night sky. Nagoji is on-model: rust-red turban, clean chin, thick moustache, gold stud, sleeves down, red sash, boots, talwar. Padmini matches her sheet. Hands and gait are sound, and there is no text or anachronism; the gunny sacks are period-plausible. Wide dark sky above and between them takes both of Padmini's balloons.

Minor only: no separate shawl (the indigo pallu drawn over the shoulder stands in for it), and the necklace is the round gold beads from her sheet rather than flat coins, which matches the sheet. The script beat is all there: roots, termite mounds, the crowd of serpent idols under the massive tree, and Revathi lighting the lamp at the largest idol. The night sky at top left is clear for both captions.

Minor: her face is lit warmly from the side and front rather than strongly from below, and the main idol here has three hoods where 12.1 has five. Otherwise on model: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, bead necklace, armlet, bindi and sandalwood line. The dark foliage at top right takes both balloons.

Small issues only. Padmini's walking stick stands upright in the leaf litter with nobody holding it, as if she drove it into the soft ground before kneeling. It reads fine but is slightly odd. Nagoji's cuffs stop a few inches above his wrists rather than at them. His inner left forearm faces his body, so no brand or scar shows. Everything else matches the script and the sheets. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, cream tunic and red sash, a sheathed talwar at his left hip, and bare feet, and he stands behind Padmini. Padmini has black hair coiled at the nape, simple gold, the cream sari with a gold border and no blouse, and she kneels with her head bowed and palms joined before the granite serpent idols. The setting matches: night under the canopy, termite mounds, roots, and one open-wick clay lamp at the largest idol. There is no text, gore or anachronism. The dark canopy in the upper middle (roughly x 0.30 to 0.65, y 0.03 to 0.30) is clear space for Padmini's balloon.

Minor: the main idol is single-hooded here where 12.1 shows five hoods; the room, lamp and night lighting are otherwise consistent. The open hand toward the idols reads clearly and the hands are sound. The night sky at top left and top centre takes both balloons.

Revathi is seen from behind, so her face is not readable. The sandalwood line is not visible from this angle. Her costume matches the sheet: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, jhumkas, coin necklace and armlets. The lamp is a small bowl, while 13.2 shows a brass lamp on a stand, a minor prop difference. There is clear dark foliage at the top centre and top left for both lines.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet, with the sandalwood line at the hairline, coin necklace, armlets and jasmine braid. She looks off to the right toward Nagoji, who is out of frame. Her hand clutching the sari is sound. The lamp is a small brass standing lamp, while the neighbouring panels show a bowl lamp, a minor difference. Lettering space is in the dark foliage at the top left and above her head.

Minor. Padmini's palms are pressed together at her forehead instead of showing the fingertips rising from the earth, which is the end point of the same gesture. Her walking stick stands upright, leaning against her forearm. Nagoji matches the bible: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, barefoot, talwar at his hip, curled moustache, clean chin and gold ear stud. Space for Padmini's line is in the dark foliage at the top centre.

Minor. This is a medium shot of Nagoji seated cross-legged rather than a close-up. The lamplight is warm from the right but does not clearly fall on only half his face. The chin and jaw carry stippled skin shading but no beard. The talwar is not visible while he sits. The turban, moustache, ear stud, barefoot feet and clasped hands are all correct. Both captions fit in the dark trees at the top left.

Minor. Revathi's fingers rest at her mouth as her composure slips, so her line will come from behind her hand, which fits the 'unsteady' tag. Nagoji's chin has light stippled shading but no beard, and his talwar is not visible while he sits. Padmini is correctly absent, and Revathi kneels alone by the lamp. Space for the lettering is in the dark canopy at the top centre, between the two figures.

Minor only. Nagoji is barefoot, which matches script 13.3 and the page 13 frames, though the ch13 bible row says boots. This is the only standing panel on the page: 14.2, 14.3 and 14.6 show the pair on the ground, so the page reads as them sinking down after the embrace. Captions fit in the dark sky and foliage at top left (left of the turban) and at top right.

Framed as a medium two-shot rather than the script's close-up, but the beat is clear: Nagoji's mouth at Revathi's jasmine-wrapped hair, both pained, her eyes closed. They sit on the ground, unlike the standing embrace in 14.1, though this matches 14.3 and 14.6. The light texture on Nagoji's jaw is the style's skin shading, not a beard (it also covers his forehead). The ear stud, moustache, rust-red turban and sash are correct, and both hands are sound. Balloons fit over the dark foliage at top left and the upper trunk.

Clean. Black trunks frame a gap of night sky with a single lit doorway at a distant tiled house, which matches the inset beat. No people and no text. The large dark-blue sky in the upper centre gives easy room for Dhanaji's short off-panel balloon. The tail points at the lit doorway, where the voice comes from.

Minor issues only. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, gold bead necklace as on the sheet, gold armlets and bangles, a sandalwood line at the hairline and no red dot. Her sad, knowing half-smile fits the beat. The damp shawl from MUST MATCH is missing. Nagoji appears from behind over the shoulder (rust turban, cream tunic, red sash, flush gold ear stud), although the prompt kept him out of frame. This still fits 'stepping close to him' and matches 14.2 and 14.3. She is seated and leaning in rather than stepping, which matches the seated staging of 14.3. The upper band is background idols, not plain dark space, but both balloons can sit over the idols at upper left and upper centre without covering her face or hands.

Minor issues only. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, a smooth chin with the sheet's light skin texture, a flush gold ear stud, rust turban, cream tunic with sleeves down, red sash, and he is barefoot. Revathi's face is at his ear with her eyes lowered, and her fingers rest on mossy stone serpent coils, so the beat reads, though her hand sits mid-right rather than strongly in the foreground. There is a tiny dark-brown inked crease between Revathi's brows below her sandalwood line. It is about 2 px wide, reads as a brow line rather than a red bindi at print size, and a retoucher can remove it if wanted. The lamp is a brass footed lamp with an open wick, which the art rules allow, but it is grander than the small clay lamp in 14.1 to 14.3. The upper-left dark sky and foliage leave plenty of clear space for the whisper balloon.

Minor only: Padmini has a small pale forehead dot that is not on her sheet. Otherwise it is on model and matches the page 14 grove. Revathi is turned to the serpent idols in her indigo and gold sari with jasmine braid and armlet. Padmini wears the cream gold-bordered sari, carries her stick and leads Nagoji. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, curled moustache, clean chin and gold ear stud. He is barefoot, carries his boots and wears his talwar. The tree trunk at top centre and the dark foliage above Padmini give room for the caption and her balloon.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor: Nagoji is in fairly full colour against the desaturated background. The dream treatment still reads, and it is close to the page 7 palette. He is alone, with no clear footprints. The horizon tilts and the fort wall is too tall and too close. The sea is flat and glassy and the palms and sand blow sideways. The open sky at upper right easily holds the caption.

Minor: the clear sky band for the three captions is a shallow strip along the top (roughly y 0 to 0.13, x 0.23 to 0.87, keeping left of the drummers at top right), but it is wide enough for three short captions and stays clear of faces and the drummer silhouettes.
